admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controllers in Kubernetes
admission-controller.md.summary: This document explains the Admission Controller mechanism, which intercepts Kubernetes API requests before object persistence. It details how these controllers can validate or mutate objects, allowing administrators to enforce policies and control resource access.

admission-policies.md.title: Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains Kubernetes declarative admission policies, which use Common Expression Language (CEL) to enforce constraints or modify resources. It details the two policy types, their binding mechanisms, and how to use parameters to customize policy behavior.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Admission Webhook Good Practices
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines essential guidelines for designing Kubernetes admission webhooks to ensure stability, performance, and reliability. It covers critical considerations such as avoiding loops, managing timeouts, and ensuring idempotent mutations.

affinity.md.title: Affinity in Kubernetes
affinity.md.summary: This document explains affinity rules in Kubernetes that guide the scheduler in placing pods. It details node affinity and pod-to-pod affinity, which are defined via labels and can be required or preferred.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Aggregation Layer Documentation
aggregation-layer.md.summary: This document explains how to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs in a cluster by configuring the API Server to support new endpoints. It details the process of adding APIService objects to claim specific URL paths.

annotation.md.title: Annotation System
annotation.md.summary: This document explains the concept of annotations as key-value pairs used to attach arbitrary metadata to objects. It details how these metadata fields can vary in size and structure, including special characters, and describes how clients retrieve this information.

api-group.md.title: Kubernetes API Group Configuration
api-group.md.summary: This document explains how to enable or disable specific API groups in Kubernetes by configuring the API server. It details how API groups are defined via REST paths and the `apiVersion` field, facilitating easier extension of the Kubernetes API.

api-resource.md.title: Kubernetes API Resource Definition
api-resource.md.summary: This document explains the Kubernetes API resource concept, which maps to endpoints on the Kubernetes API server. It details how resources define object schemas and support operations like permissions.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: This document outlines security vulnerabilities where attackers can bypass Kubernetes API server controls, including static pod manipulation and direct kubelet API access. It details specific bypass mechanisms and provides mitigation strategies for cluster operators and security architects.

app-container.md.title: Pod App Containers
app-container.md.summary: This document explains the concept of application containers within Kubernetes pods, which run after init containers complete. It clarifies that app containers handle the main application logic, while init containers manage startup tasks that do not persist after execution.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect
application-architect.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Application Architect, who designs high-level system architectures to ensure scalability and maintainability. It explains how architects coordinate with surrounding components such as databases, logging infrastructure, and microservices.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Kubernetes Application Security Checklist
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This document provides a developer-focused guide for securing applications running in Kubernetes. It covers base hardening, service accounts, pod and container-level security contexts, RBAC, image security, network policies, and advanced hardening strategies.

approver.md.title: Kubernetes Code Contribution Approval Process
approver.md.summary: This document defines the role of an Approver, who reviews code contributions beyond basic quality checks to ensure holistic acceptance. It explains that approval covers compatibility, API adherence, performance, and system interactions, distinguishing it from the broader code review process.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture Overview
architecture.md.summary: This document details the components of a Kubernetes cluster, including the control plane (kube-apiserver, etcd, scheduler, etc.) and worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy). It explains how these systems manage workloads, handle network traffic, and ensure high availability across multiple nodes.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide - Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This document outlines Kubernetes authentication mechanisms, including X.509 client certificates, static token files, and service account tokens. It explains the security implications, limitations, and best practices for each method to ensure cluster security.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization
authorization.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes API requests are evaluated for access control, detailing the default deny policy, the sequence of authorization module checks, and the specific request attributes (user, group, API, verb, etc.) used to make authorization decisions.

autoscaling.md.title: Autoscaling Workloads in Kubernetes
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes manages workload scaling through manual and automatic methods. It details horizontal scaling via HorizontalPodAutoscalers and vertical scaling via VerticalPodAutoscalers, including in-place pod resizing and cluster size-based configurations.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor: Container Resource Monitoring
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that tracks resource usage, performance metrics, and network statistics for running containers. It aggregates historical data and exports these metrics for container and machine-wide analysis.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI) Specification
cdi.md.summary: This document explains the Container Device Interface (CDI), a Kubernetes specification for configuring devices within containers. It details how CDI enables workloads to access hardware resources via device plugins and dynamic resource allocation.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL) in Kubernetes
cel.md.summary: This document explains the Common Expression Language (CEL), a fast and safe expression system for Kubernetes. It details how CEL enables dynamic admission control and resource allocation by filtering requests and selecting resources based on specific attributes.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes API Access Certificates
certificate.md.summary: This document explains the role of certificates in securing Kubernetes API access. It details how these cryptographically secure files validate client identities and ensure only authorized applications can interact with the cluster.

cgroup.md.title: Linux cgroup (Control Group) Overview
cgroup.md.summary: This document explains the Linux cgroup feature, which isolates and limits resource usage (CPU, memory, I/O) for collections of processes. It details how cgroups manage accounting and enforce resource constraints on system resources.

cidr.md.title: Understanding CIDR in Kubernetes Networking
cidr.md.summary: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) is a protocol for defining IP address blocks, essential for Kubernetes to assign unique IPs to Pods. This document explains how CIDR notation enables Node-to-Pod IP allocation and covers both IPv4 and IPv6 support.

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA) Overview
cla.md.summary: This document explains the Contributor License Agreement, a legal framework that allows contributors to grant licenses for their open source contributions. It clarifies how CLAs resolve disputes regarding intellectual property rights and ensures compliance with open source terms.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager: Kubernetes Cloud Integration
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: This document explains the Cloud Controller Manager (CCM), a Kubernetes control plane component that bridges the cluster and cloud provider APIs. It details how CCM separates cloud-specific logic from core cluster components, allowing providers to release features independently of the main Kubernetes project.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security and Kubernetes Lifecycle
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document outlines the CNCF's cloud native security framework, detailing how Kubernetes secures the development, distribution, deployment, and runtime phases of cloud-native applications. It emphasizes supply chain protection, threat modeling, and access controls to ensure a secure platform.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider Definition and Managed Services
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines a cloud provider as an organization offering cloud computing platforms, distinguishing between Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS). It explains that managed IaaS involves the provider handling servers and storage while users manage applications, and managed PaaS includes the provider's responsibility for the Kubernetes control plane and infrastructure.

cluster-administration.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Administration Guide
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document provides an overview for Kubernetes administrators covering cluster planning, node management, resource quotas, and security configurations including certificate generation and API access control.

cluster-operations.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Operations Guide
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document outlines the daily management and coordination tasks required to maintain a Kubernetes cluster, including node deployment, software upgrades, security configuration, and observability.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator: Definition and Responsibilities
cluster-operator.md.summary: This document defines the Cluster Operator as a role responsible for configuring, controlling, and monitoring Kubernetes clusters. It outlines their primary duties, including maintaining cluster stability and executing periodic maintenance or upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster Architecture and Components
cluster.md.summary: This document explains the structure of a containerized application cluster, detailing how worker nodes host Pods while the control plane manages them for fault tolerance and high availability.

cncf.md.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Overview
cncf.md.summary: The CNCF is a Linux Foundation sub-foundation dedicated to building sustainable ecosystems for containerized microservices. It promotes the use of Kubernetes as a core technology to make cloud native computing ubiquitous.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI) Plugins
cni.md.summary: This document explains Container Network Interface (CNI) plugins, which adhere to the appc/CNI specification. It details how these plugins enable networking for containers within Kubernetes environments.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Components Overview
components.md.summary: This document outlines the essential components of a Kubernetes cluster, including the control plane, node components, and optional addons. It details the roles of core services like kube-apiserver and etcd, as well as runtime nodes such as kubelet and kube-proxy.

condition.md.title: Understanding Kubernetes Resource Conditions
condition.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes resources define their current state through 'conditions' within their status. It details the structure of these conditions, including their type, status, and optional fields like reason and message, using Pod examples such as Ready and ContainersReady.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Methods
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes separates configuration from code using ConfigMaps, Secrets, and container helpers like sidecars and init containers.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: This document explains container environment variables as name=value pairs that supply essential information to running containers. It details how these variables support applications by providing details about the container, file systems, and cluster resources.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime in Kubernetes
container-runtime.md.summary: This document explains the role of the Container Runtime as a fundamental component for executing and managing containers within the Kubernetes environment. It details supported runtimes like containerd and cri-o, as well as the Kubernetes CRI interface that enables these implementations.

container.md.title: Container Definition and Overview
container.md.summary: This document defines a container as a lightweight executable image containing software and dependencies. It explains how containers decouple applications from host infrastructure to simplify deployment and scaling across various cloud environments.

containerd.md.title: Container Runtime Overview
containerd.md.summary: This document explains containerd, a lightweight container runtime designed for simplicity and portability. It details how containerd manages image storage, container execution, and network access on Linux and Windows systems.

containers.md.title: Containers and Container Images
containers.md.summary: This document explains the concept of containers, their role in decoupling applications from infrastructure, and the distinction between container images and runtimes. It details how container images provide stateless, immutable software packages while runtime classes manage execution environments within Kubernetes.

contributor.md.title: Contributor Roles and Activities in Kubernetes
contributor.md.summary: This document defines the various ways individuals contribute to the Kubernetes project, including code donations, documentation, and community engagement. It outlines specific activities such as pull requests, issue reporting, and participation in Special Interest Groups (SIGs).

control-plane.md.title: Container Orchestration Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: This document explains the control plane layer responsible for defining, deploying, and managing container lifecycles. It details the key components including etcd, API Server, Scheduler, Controller Manager, and Cloud Controller Manager, which can operate as OS daemons or containers.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configuring CPU Resource Limits for Kubernetes Namespaces
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This guide explains how to set minimum and maximum CPU constraints using a LimitRange object within a Kubernetes namespace. It details the process of creating a namespace, defining a LimitRange with default and max limits, and verifying that Pods within the namespace adhere to these constraints.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configuring Default CPU Resources for Kubernetes Namespaces
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This guide explains how to set default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace using LimitRange and Pod manifests. It details how the control plane assigns default values when containers do not specify their own resource constraints.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O: Kubernetes Container Runtime Interface
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a tool that enables Kubernetes to utilize OCI-compliant container runtimes, allowing it to execute Pods and pull images from remote registries.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob: Creating Scheduled Jobs
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains how to define a CronJob, which is a system component that schedules recurring tasks like backups or reports. It details the required schedule syntax, job creation steps, concurrency policies, and common limitations.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI) Overview
csi.md.summary: This document explains the Container Storage Interface (CSI), which provides a standard interface for Kubernetes to expose storage systems. It details how vendors can deploy out-of-tree CSI drivers to create custom storage classes without modifying the Kubernetes repository.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition: Kubernetes Custom API Objects
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: This document explains CustomResourceDefinitions, which allow Kubernetes clusters to extend their API server with custom resources. It details how these objects enable the creation of new API resources without requiring a full custom server implementation.

daemonset.md.title: Understanding DaemonSets in Kubernetes
daemonset.md.summary: This document explains how to create and manage DaemonSets, which ensure specific Pods run on every node in a cluster. It covers the required YAML structure, pod templates, selectors, and scheduling behaviors.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Containerized Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for resolving issues with containerized applications, including guidance on Kubernetes resources like Pods and Services, and strategies for interpreting container termination messages.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Kubernetes Cluster Nodes
debug-cluster.md.summary: This guide explains how to diagnose and resolve issues with Kubernetes cluster nodes, including checking node registration, inspecting node health via logs, and understanding failure modes.

debug.md.title: Kubernetes Debugging and Troubleshooting Guide
debug.md.summary: This document provides resources for users and administrators to gather information and resolve issues when things go wrong in Kubernetes environments. It covers debugging applications, cluster management, logging, and monitoring, along with community support options.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployments: Declarative Updates and Rollout Management
deployment.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes Deployments provide a declarative way to manage Pod and ReplicaSet states. It details the process of creating Deployments, updating them via labels, and managing rollout strategies such as rolling updates, pausing, and scaling.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin Overview
device-plugin.md.summary: This document explains how device plugins enable Kubernetes workloads to access hardware resources on worker nodes. It details deployment methods, such as daemonsets, and describes the mechanism by which plugins advertise infrastructure features to kubelets.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugin Framework in Kubernetes
device-plugins.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes allows vendors to register hardware resources like GPUs and NICs via a device plugin framework. It details the registration process using gRPC, the resource naming scheme, and how these resources are advertised to the kubelet and API server.

device.md.title: Device Resources in Kubernetes
device.md.summary: This document defines infrastructure resources attached to nodes, including commercial hardware like GPUs and custom ASIC boards. It explains that these devices require specific device drivers to enable Kubernetes Pods to access them.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass and ResourceClaims
deviceclass.md.summary: This document explains how DeviceClasses define groups of devices for workload allocation, which are then claimed via ResourceClaims based on specific device parameters.

disruption.md.title: Understanding Pod Disruptions in Kubernetes
disruption.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes defines disruptions as events causing Pods to go out of service, distinguishing between voluntary and involuntary causes like Node failures or application destruction.

dns-pod-service.md.title: DNS Configuration for Kubernetes Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes assigns DNS names to Services and Pods, enabling service discovery. It details record types like A/AAAA and SRV records, and describes how the DNS search domain list is configured via the Pod's hostname and subdomain fields.
